posts.title: Opening a Company in Turkey for Foreigners
posts.summary:
Foreign investors can form a Turkish company, but the process has clear legal steps: company type, capital, MERSİS registration, tax office and bank account. Our English guide walks through the essentials for non-residents.

Read the full guide:
https://cindemirlaw.com/opening-a-company-in-turkey-for-foreigners/

posts.title: Deportation Law In Turkey
posts.summary:
Deportation decisions in Türkiye follow the Law on Foreigners and International Protection. Foreign nationals have procedural rights — including objection and stay of execution in many cases. Know the grounds and timelines.

Full article:
https://cindemirlaw.com/deportation-law-in-turkey/

posts.title: Debt Collection in Turkey
posts.summary:
Recovering a debt in Türkiye may involve enforcement offices, mandatory mediation and court action. Foreign creditors should also plan for power of attorney and security deposit rules.

Practical overview:
https://cindemirlaw.com/debt-recovery-in-turkey/

posts.title: Consensual Divorce in Turkey
posts.summary:
Uncontested (consensual) divorce in Türkiye is faster when spouses agree on custody, property and support in a settlement protocol. Useful for foreign spouses with ties to Turkish courts.

Guide:
https://cindemirlaw.com/consensual-divorce-in-turkey-uncontested-divorce/

posts.title: Criminal Record Certificate in Turkey
posts.summary:
A Turkish criminal record (police clearance) certificate is often required for visas, residence, citizenship or employment abroad. Here is how foreigners request and use it.

Step-by-step:
https://cindemirlaw.com/getting-criminal-record-in-turkey/

posts.title: Airport Detention in Turkey
posts.summary:
Passport control or customs issues at Istanbul airports can turn into detention for foreign travellers. Knowing your rights — and when to call counsel — matters in the first hours.

Read more:
https://cindemirlaw.com/airport-detention-in-turkey-legal-risks-for-foreign-travellers-and-how-to-respond/

posts.title: Real Estate for Foreigners in Turkey
posts.summary:
Foreign buyers face military-zone restrictions, title deed checks and currency rules when purchasing property in Türkiye. A clear legal checklist reduces closing risk.

Article:
https://cindemirlaw.com/sales-of-real-estate-to-foreigners-in-turkey/

posts.title: Enforcing a Foreign Judgment in Turkey
posts.summary:
A foreign court decision is not automatically enforceable in Türkiye. Recognition and enforcement (tenfiz) require a Turkish court application with specific documents.

Guide:
https://cindemirlaw.com/enforcement-of-a-foreign-decision-in-turkey/

posts.title: Airport Customs Seizures under Turkish Law
posts.summary:
What begins as a routine customs check can become a formal seizure or smuggling investigation. Travellers should understand the legal thresholds and defence options.

Full analysis:
https://cindemirlaw.com/airport-customs-seizures-and-smuggling-offences-under-turkish-law/

posts.title: How to Lift an Entry Ban to Turkey
posts.summary:
An entry ban may follow deportation — or be issued by Migration Management without removal. Foreign nationals can apply to lift or shorten the ban under Turkish law.

Details:
https://cindemirlaw.com/how-to-lift-entry-ban-to-turkey/

posts.summary:

posts.summary:
Russian nationals can still form Turkish companies. Sanctions pressure makes structure, banking and nominee arrangements especially important — done lawfully.
